skills.name: Writing responsible slogans about sexual health

note.text: A slogan is a brief memorable message for an audience. For health topics, it must also be accurate, respectful and free of stigma. A slogan cannot diagnose an infection or replace professional advice. Avoid false guarantees, blame or frightening claims. A useful message can encourage credible information, respectful choices and access to trained care. Discuss classroom suitability with the teacher; pupils do not need to reveal private experiences for this writing task.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: A slogan is a brief memorable message for an audience. For health topics, it must also be accurate, respectful and free of stigma. A slogan cannot diagnose an infection or replace professional advice. Avoid false guarantees, blame or frightening claims. A useful message can encourage credible information, respectful choices and access to trained care. Discuss classroom suitability with the teacher; pupils do not need to reveal private experiences for this writing task.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original model: Original model slogans: Get the facts; seek trained care. Respect privacy, support health. Ask a health professional, not a rumour. These messages encourage informed help-seeking without labelling or shaming a person. A teacher can discuss which wording is suitable for a school audience.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Choose one action and express it concisely. Check the factual claim and the audience. Remove any suggestion that a person's worth depends on health status or that an English slogan guarantees prevention. Reread for rhythm and spelling without sacrificing accuracy.

paper_task.prompt: Draft original, respectful school slogans about getting reliable STI information or trained health advice. Do not include private experiences or unsupported treatment/prevention guarantees.
model: Original model slogans: Get the facts; seek trained care. Respect privacy, support health. Ask a health professional, not a rumour. These messages encourage informed help-seeking without labelling or shaming a person. A teacher can discuss which wording is suitable for a school audience.
checklist: Each message is short and focused.
I avoid stigma, blame and false guarantees.
I identify a suitable audience and a credible help-seeking action.
